title: The ship of Theseus
examples: If I replace all my clothes, am I still me?
Does something need to stay exactly the same to keep its identity?
What makes a person the same person over time?

explain.say: Today we look at a puzzle about what stays the same.
The puzzle asks if an object keeps its identity through change.
Imagine replacing every single plank of the ship one by one.
If we rebuild it with the old planks, is that the real ship?
This shows that identity is not just about the parts.

items: It relates to form or function

explain.say: Think about your own body changing over many years.

faq.q: Does the material matter for identity?
faq.a: Some philosophers say that the original material is very important. Others argue that the form or pattern is what matters more.
asks: Is the stuff it's made of important?
Does it have to be the same stuff?

faq.q: If I change my mind, does my identity change?
faq.a: This brings up questions about mental continuity. Some argue that memory and consciousness are key to personal identity.
asks: Is it just my thoughts that define me?

faq.q: Is there one single answer to this puzzle?
faq.a: No, this is a classic thought experiment designed to show that there is no single, easy answer. It makes us think deeply.
asks: Can I solve this with a simple rule?
Is this just a trick question?

faq.q: What is the difference between physical and personal identity?
faq.a: Physical identity relates to the body's matter, while personal identity relates to the self or consciousness over time.
asks: Do I have to keep my body to keep my self?

faq.q: Can this puzzle be applied to technology?
faq.a: Yes, we can think about software updates or AI. If a program is rewritten completely, is it the same program?

facts: The Ship of Theseus is a famous thought experiment.
It questions the concept of persistence through change.
It explores the relationship between matter and form.
It suggests identity might be more abstract than physical.

quiz.say: If a statue is carved from marble and all the marble is replaced over time, what is the main philosophical question raised?

options.show: It must have the original builders.
options.say: It must have the original builders.

options.show: Is it still the same statue?
options.say: Is it still the same statue?

options.show: It must be the original marble.
options.say: It must be the original marble.

options.show: It must look exactly the same.
options.say: It must look exactly the same.

quiz.why: The experiment forces us to consider what makes something recognizable over time.

wrong.0: The builders are not part of the physical object's identity.
wrong.2: This is too strict because it ignores how things naturally wear down.
wrong.3: Appearance can change even if the core identity remains.

quiz.say: When considering personal identity, what aspect is often considered crucial?
quiz.why: Many theories suggest that our continuous stream of memories links us to our past selves.

wrong.0: We change our appearance, but we feel like the same person.
wrong.1: Our cells constantly replace themselves, so the DNA changes too.
wrong.2: Identity is usually seen as a pattern over time, not just one moment.

quiz.say: If a river flows constantly, always carrying new water, what does this suggest about identity?

options.show: It must be the same water molecules.
options.say: It must be the same water molecules.

options.show: It must have the same banks.
options.say: It must have the same banks.

options.show: It must be contained in a specific container.
options.say: It must be contained in a specific container.

quiz.why: The river always flows, suggesting that process or function can maintain identity.

wrong.1: The water molecules are always moving and changing.
wrong.2: While the banks are constant, the water itself is not.
wrong.3: The river's identity is defined by its flow, not just its banks.
